We are delighted to welcome you to the website for our brilliant, inclusive and unique school.
Welcome to Gladstone Park Primary School. A member of Anthem Schools Trust, we are a welcoming, vibrant and friendly school situated in the heart of Brent, North London. At Gladstone Park, we develop resilient, emotionally-intelligent students who become life-long learners.
We aim to ensure that all children receive an exciting, relevant and knowledge-rich curriculum which fosters a life-long love of learning and prepares them for the modern world. We wholeheartedly promote a stimulating and positive learning environment where all our children feel happy, safe and valued as individuals through our 'RIDER' values: respect, integrity, determination, empathy and responsibility.
Gladstone Park Primary School,Sherrick Green Road,London, NW10 1LB

Art and DT
Our Art and Design Technology curriculum at Gladstone Park is ambitious and carefully structured to ensure all pupils develop the essential knowledge and practical skills needed to succeed and think creatively. We follow a split curriculum in which pupils study either Art or Design Technology each half term, allowing time for focused, in-depth learning within each subject. Our curriculum is both knowledge- and skills-based and is designed to be progressive over time, so that pupils can build securely on prior learning and make meaningful connections between what they have learned in previous years and the subject they are studying at the time. Across both subjects, children are given regular, high-quality practical opportunities to design, create, experiment and refine their work, enabling skills to be practised and mastered with increasing confidence.
Enrichment plays a vital role in our curriculum, and we are proud to be working with Camden Arts Centre to enhance pupils’ experiences and engagement with the arts. Experiences such as these form part of our Gladstone Park Pledge, which is reviewed regularly to ensure our curriculum is enriched with purposeful opportunities for creative exploration, hands-on design and making, and meaningful engagement with our local community and London.
DT School Overview

History & Geography
History
At Gladstone Park Primary School, we are ambitious for every child to develop a deep understanding of the past and to begin their journey as confident, curious historians. Our history curriculum is built around the knowledge-rich Pearson programme, which is carefully structured to ensure that both knowledge and skills develop progressively over time. This means that pupils continually build on what they have learned before, making meaningful connections between previous periods of history and the topics they are studying in the present. Through this coherent and cumulative approach, children are supported to retain key knowledge, see patterns across time and grow in confidence as historians.
Alongside substantive knowledge – the key facts, events, people and concepts that children need to know about different historical periods – we explicitly teach disciplinary knowledge, which helps pupils understand how historians work. This includes learning how to ask and answer historical questions, analyse sources and evidence, identify cause and consequence, recognise similarities and differences, and understand change and continuity over time. In the Early Years, history is taught through Understanding the World, where children begin to develop a sense of the past and present, talk about their own lives and experiences, and explore ideas of time and age. In Years 1 and 2, pupils study history across three terms, allowing them to explore topics in depth and develop secure foundations of knowledge and historical thinking. In Years 3 to 6, history is taught in Autumn 1, Spring 1 and Summer 1, enabling pupils to revisit and build upon prior learning as their understanding becomes more sophisticated.
Assessment is an integral part of our history teaching. Teachers continuously check pupils’ understanding of both substantive knowledge and disciplinary skills through quizzing, high-quality questioning and feedback in books. Each unit of work culminates in an assessment where pupils are expected to draw on what they know and use the skills of a historian to answer an enquiry-based question. Alongside classroom learning, we enrich our curriculum through a carefully planned calendar of trips, visitors and events linked directly to the history topics studied. These experiences form part of our Gladstone Park Pledge and reflect our commitment to providing meaningful opportunities for pupils to engage with the past locally, within our community, and across London. This offer is reviewed regularly to ensure our curriculum remains ambitious, relevant and inspiring for all our children.
Geography
At Gladstone Park Primary School, we are ambitious for every child to develop a deep understanding of the world around them and to grow into confident, curious geographers. Our geography curriculum follows the knowledge-rich Pearson programme, which is carefully structured to ensure that both knowledge and skills build progressively over time. This allows pupils to make clear connections between what they have learned in previous years and the places, themes and issues they are studying in the present. Through this cumulative approach, children deepen their understanding of physical and human geography and develop a strong sense of how the world is interconnected.
Alongside substantive knowledge – the key facts, concepts and vocabulary about places, environments and geographical features – we explicitly teach procedural knowledge, which focuses on how geography is done. This includes learning how to use maps, atlases, globes, aerial photographs and digital mapping tools; collecting, interpreting and presenting data; and carrying out fieldwork to observe, measure and record geographical information. In addition, we teach disciplinary knowledge so pupils learn how to think like geographers: asking geographical questions, explaining patterns and processes, understanding cause and effect, and forming reasoned conclusions about the world. In the Early Years, geography is taught through Understanding the World, where children explore their immediate environment, develop positional and directional language, and learn about similarities and differences between places. In Years 1 and 2, pupils study geography across all three terms, allowing them time to build secure foundations, revisit key concepts and develop confidence in essential geographical knowledge and skills. In Years 3 to 6, geography is taught in Autumn 2, Spring 2 and Summer 2, enabling pupils to revisit and build upon prior learning as their geographical understanding becomes increasingly sophisticated.
Assessment is embedded throughout our geography teaching. Teachers continuously check pupils’ understanding of substantive, procedural and disciplinary knowledge through regular quizzing, questioning and feedback in lessons and books. Each unit concludes with an assessment where pupils are expected to apply their knowledge and skills to answer an enquiry-based question. These assessments also require pupils to demonstrate their geographical literacy, including accurate use of subject-specific vocabulary, maps, diagrams, data and explanations. Alongside classroom learning, our geography curriculum is enriched through a carefully planned programme of trips, fieldwork and events linked to the topics studied. These experiences form part of our Gladstone Park Pledge and reflect our commitment to providing meaningful opportunities for pupils to explore their local area, engage with their community, and deepen their understanding of London and the wider world.

Maths
At Gladstone Park, we are ambitious for all pupils to develop a deep, secure and flexible understanding of mathematics that prepares them for future learning and everyday life. In the Early Years, we follow the Effective Maths Programme, which builds strong foundations in children’s understanding of number and early mathematical concepts, setting them up for success as they transition into Year 1. From Year 1 to Year 6, our maths curriculum is underpinned by White Rose Maths, ensuring learning is carefully sequenced and progressive over time. Lessons are personalised through our six-part lesson structure, which provides explicit teaching of new methods in their simplest form, followed by a gradual handover of responsibility as pupils build confidence and independence. We embed the concrete, pictorial and abstract (CPA) approach across all year groups, giving children regular opportunities to work with manipulatives to support understanding and make mathematical concepts meaningful. Oracy is a key feature of every lesson, enabling pupils to explain their thinking, use precise mathematical language and learn from one another, and pupils are regularly challenged to deepen their understanding through problem-solving and reasoning opportunities.

Music
At Gladstone Park Primary School, we recognise the importance of music in supporting pupils’ creativity and personal development. Music is an integral part of our curriculum, and we ensure that all pupils have opportunities to enjoy, explore and create music.
Pupils develop their skills through singing, playing instruments and listening to a wide range of music from different cultures, historical periods and traditions. This enables them to build confidence, work collaboratively and develop their creativity.
Our curriculum is designed to foster a lifelong appreciation of music, while developing pupils’ musical knowledge and skills progressively across the school.
In Early Years and Key Stage 1, teachers deliver music using the Charanga programme. In KS2, specialist teachers from Brent Music Service provide high-quality music tuition. All pupils take part in regular singing assemblies and termly performances.
Additional opportunities are provided through Brent Music Service, where pupils can access instrumental lessons in violin, guitar and keyboard. We also work with Rocksteady, which delivers in-school band sessions that promote teamwork, confidence and a sense of belonging.
The school choir is a particular strength. It is of a high standard and represents the school successfully at a range of events across London.

Science
Our science curriculum is designed to spark curiosity and develop children’s understanding of the world through exploration and enquiry. We follow the White Rose Science curriculum, which is fully aligned with the National Curriculum and places strong emphasis on Working Scientifically skills. This gives our children regular opportunities to investigate scientific concepts through hands-on experiments and practical learning. The curriculum is carefully sequenced to build on prior learning, with a strong focus on key vocabulary so that children can confidently talk about their learning using scientific language. We assess the pupil’s science knowledge through end of unit assessments, capturing what they have learnt and giving teachers an accurate judgement of their attainment. As part of the Gladstone Park Pledge, meaningful links to outdoor learning are woven throughout the curriculum, providing children with even more opportunities to explore, observe and learn beyond the classroom.

SEND and inclusion
Ensuring every child achieves
We are committed to ensuring that every child receives an education that enables them to grow as successful learners and members of our community.
We understand that pupils learn in different ways and at difference paces, and aim to support all pupils to participate in school life and learning to the best of their individual abilities.
At Gladstone Park, we understand that some pupils need more support than others to achieve. Many pupils may need help throughout their time in education, while others may need a little extra support for a short period to help them overcome more temporary problems.
During this time they will be part of our Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Register, and we will keep a close eye on their progress.
Children on the SEND register have individual targets which focus on their next steps in learning. Progress summaries are shared with parents regularly throughout the year.
All pupils have access to the curriculum. They are supported through quality first teaching and suitable adjustments that are personalised to the individual child.
The school’s SEND coordinator (SENDCo) is Marcela Skoupilova. If you are concerned about your child, or would like some advice, please contact her at mskoupilova@gladpark.anthemtrust.uk

Reading
Early Reading
At Gladstone Park, we are highly ambitious for all pupils to become confident, fluent and enthusiastic readers. Our phonics curriculum is underpinned by Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which provides a systematic, rigorous and highly effective approach to teaching phonics. From the very start of their reading journey, children are taught the phonics knowledge and skills they need to decode accurately through daily, structured lessons that build progressively over time. Learning is carefully sequenced so that pupils can securely apply new sounds, practise blending and segmenting, and revisit prior learning, enabling them to make strong connections and develop fluency. Children regularly read fully decodable books that are closely matched to the phonics they have been taught, ensuring early success, growing confidence and a secure foundation for reading with understanding and enjoyment.
In EYFS, we love sharing stories and developing a lifelong love of reading. Children have daily opportunities to explore a wide range of books, listen to stories, talk about their favourite characters and retell familiar tales through play.
Our inviting reading areas encourage children to choose books independently and enjoy quiet moments with a story. We also have a dedicated EYFS library, where children can choose a book to take home and share with their families. This gives children the opportunity to select books that interest them and helps to build a positive connection between reading at school and reading at home.
Through reading for pleasure, children develop their imagination, vocabulary, communication skills and understanding of the world around them.
We encourage families to enjoy these books together by talking about the pictures, discussing the story and simply enjoying the special experience of sharing a book. Children often love hearing their favourite stories again and again!
Y2-6 Reading
Our reading curriculum is built on high ambition and the belief that every child can become a confident, lifelong reader. We follow the Literacy Tree curriculum, which is carefully structured to ensure that knowledge and skills are taught progressively over time, allowing pupils to make meaningful connections with what they have learned in previous years through rich and exciting texts. In Key Stage 1, we use Little Wandle as our phonics programme, giving our youngest readers a strong foundation in decoding and early reading skills. From Years 2 to 6, reading lessons follow a clear structure that explicitly teaches strategies to help pupils comprehend and engage deeply with a wide range of texts. Each term, pupils complete summative reading assessments that focus on phonics, fluency and comprehension, ensuring we can support every child to make strong progress as they grow into skilled and enthusiastic readers.

Nursery
Children are entitled to at least 15 hours' free provision in nursery, starting at the beginning of the term following their third birthday. We can also offer up to an additional 15 hours for parents entitled to the Extended Hours Funding, which means a total of 30 hours of free Nursery provision. Parents who are not entitled to Extended Hours Funding can pay for additional hours themselves. Please see below timings and costing options for parents.
Gladstone Park Nursery is always a busy and fun place to be! The indoor and outdoor learning environments are bright and spacious giving all children the opportunity to explore and learn in their play.
Our Nursery is part of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) within the primary school. Activities and resources are carefully planned to provide a rich variety of first-hand learning opportunities and experiences that encourage children to show interest, curiosity, and enthusiasm – the beginnings of lifelong learning.
If you would like to apply for a Nursery place, please contact the school office for an application form on 0208 452 1350 or by email at admin@gladpark.anthemtrust.uk
Please note that attendance at a school nursery does not automatically entitle your child to a place in Reception at that school, so if you would like your child to join the Reception class at Gladstone Park, you must apply for a place through Brent Council, even if they already attend the Nursery.
See the Admissions page of this website for further details.

Computing
Our computing curriculum is designed to equip children with the knowledge and skills they need to thrive in an ever-changing digital world. We follow the NCCE Computing curriculum, ensuring learning is progressive, purposeful and aligned with national expectations. This journey begins in Key Stage 1, where our youngest learners explore the technology all around them and take their first steps into programming by controlling robots. In Lower Key Stage 2, children develop their creativity and technical skills through activities such as stop-frame animation and photo editing. By Upper Key Stage 2, pupils build on this foundation to program their own games and begin working with 3D modelling, preparing them with confidence, creativity and problem-solving skills for the future.

Joining us in Reception from September 2026
We are delighted that your child will be joining our school’s Reception team in September, and we are looking forward to getting, or in many cases, continuing to get to know them! Starting school should be a happy and exciting time for both your child and you. We know that you will have lots of questions to ask us and hope the information included will begin to answer at least some of those questions.
We will do our very best to make you and your child feel secure and valued and ready for the start of the new school year. Our aim is to provide your child with the very best education possible and we hope that you will work in partnership with us, to achieve this aim.
Parent/child interview:
Prior to the start of the Reception year, you will need to attend a parent/child interview. This will be a time for Reception staff to find out more about you and your child and to help them settle better. This will also be an opportunity to ask questions or discuss any concerns. If you have more sensitive matters that you would need to discuss with the Early Years lead and SENDCo, you will have the opportunity to meet them during the interview if you have not already been contacted.
Our doors open at 8:30am and stay open until 8:40am. Please ensure children arrive on time – we encourage children to arrive as early as possible so that they can access early morning activity. The day ends at 3.15pm.
For a smooth transition, we are providing staggered entry. Children in year reception will start 2nd of September in groups of 7 children a day. Children will stay full day 8.45-15.15.
Your child is welcome to have school dinners – we provide halal dinners. If you wish your child to have a packed lunch from home, you must ensure this is nut-free, healthy and with only water to drink. At break time, the children are encouraged to have a piece of fruit or vegetable with a quarter of a bagel in the morning and milk in the afternoon. All is provided by the school free of charge. Your child can drink water during the day. We recommend reusable water bottles, and please make sure your child’s name is clearly labeled.
You will need to ensure that your child has all the uniform items before joining. You will be informed which day will be PE day when you start.
We are Proud to Announce our new Uniform Supplier for Gladstone Park Primary School is Ace Clothing.
To order uniform Online kindly use the link below
https://www.aceclothing.co.uk/school-uniform/gladstone-park-primary-school
You can also visit the store:
Opening Hours Monday to Friday 9.30am to 5.00pm
5A Courtenay Road East Lane Business Park East Lane Wembley
info@aceclothing.co.uk
Other, non-branded items of school uniform can be purchased from a wide range of high street and second-hand retailers and are acceptable as part of school uniform. We have a limited supply of second-hand uniform at school for families in financial difficulties: please contact our welfare officer.
What Your Child Needs for School
Your child will need a set of spare clothes that will be kept in school so they can change if they get wet or have an accident. Please also provide wellington boots for outdoor play. All items must be clearly labelled with your child’s name.
The school provides puddle suits for every child, allowing them to take part in outdoor learning even in wet weather.
Each child should bring a school bag, preferably a book bag, which is large enough to hold A4 folders and school work comfortably.
We cannot stress enough the importance of labelling all your child’s belongings.
Reading and Learning:
At our school, we use a range of high-quality programmes to support your child’s learning and development:
Phonics and Early Reading – We follow the Little Wandle phonics scheme to support children in developing strong reading and writing skills.
Literacy – We use Literacy Tree to inspire a love of reading and develop writing through high-quality texts.
Mathematics – We use Effective Maths to build a strong understanding of numbers and problem-solving skills.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSHE) – We follow the Jigsaw programme to support children’s wellbeing and relationships.
Music – We use Kapow to provide engaging and creative music lessons.
Class Library books – changed once a week on Tuesday (these books are for parents to read to their children or just look at the pictures and talk about them).
Online reading Collins - online reading one phonic book that your child already practised at school for 3 sessions.
Online math – numbots platform 5min a day.
Handwriting practise – worksheet every Friday
Login for your child will be in their reading record. Reading record books need to be kept in your child’s bag all the time!
Parent Staff Association
The Parent Staff Association (PSA) is a registered charity whose primary purpose is to fundraise for those little extras outside the school’s budget. Keeping children safe online
At our school, this can include computers, laptops and tablet computers, and at home it can also include devices such as games consoles (Xbox, Playstation, Nintendo Switch), mobile phones and anything else which allows interactive digital communication.
The online environment is an integral part of children’s lives, so it is important that we work together as a school community to ensure that our children have a healthy relationship with technology and support them to use it responsibly.
For more useful advice and guidance about keeping children safe online, visit the NSPCC online safety website.
NSPCC Online safety website
Social media
Increasingly, children are using social media apps - there are so many now that it can be difficult to keep up! There are lots of benefits for children and young people when using social media. This includes staying connected with friends and family, enabling innovative ways of learning and creating new ways for them to express themselves. But there are also risks of allowing children access to social media, some of which are outlined below.
Children may be exposed to upsetting or inappropriate content online, particularly if the platform they are using doesn’t have robust privacy and security settings or if you’re not checking posts. This content might be sexually explicit, or it might be harmful in other ways, such as radicalisation, bullying, or content that's upsetting.
Children may be at risk of being groomed if they have an online profile that means they can be contacted privately.
Children’s posts or profile information may expose personal information and put them at risk. For example, they may talk about their home life, feelings, or thoughts they’ve been having. There may be information that makes them identifiable, such as locations of events they are taking part in, or visual clues in photographs. Perpetrators may use this information to groom, abuse or exploit children.
Perpetrators of abuse may create fake profiles to try to contact children and young people through the platform you’re using, for example an adult posing as a child. They may also create anonymous accounts and engage in cyberbullying or trolling. People known to a child can also perpetrate abuse.
On many platforms, children can be contacted anywhere and at any time through private messaging or notification alerts. This means it’s harder for them to escape from abusive messages or upsetting content that they are tagged in.
Further advice for parents can be found on the following websites:
thinkyouknow for parents and carers
Talking to your child about online sexual harassment
UK safer internet centre advice for parents and carers

Latin
At Gladstone Park Primary School, we have chosen to teach Latin, a fascinating ancient language that affords our children rich learning opportunities.
We want to stimulate children’s natural curiosity through our knowledge-based curriculum and encourage each and every child in our care to develop a passion and a love of language, where they are not only able to learn a new language, but also gain a better understanding of their own.
Teaching our chosen ancient language, Latin, and using the literacy-rich approach provided by Maximum Classics, we seek to encourage all our children to be confident, critical thinkers who are reflective about the development of languages and how Latin has influenced and impacted the way we read, write and speak today.
We aim to guide all our children towards becoming compassionate, responsible individuals, who respect and celebrate our cultural and linguistic heritage and have the foundations needed to confidently tackle the challenge of learning modern foreign languages at KS3.
